tools.name: council_status
tools.description: Where the council stands for your seat: the agenda item, any pending motion, what happened since you last looked, and — if a round is open for you — exactly what you may submit, with reasons. Never blocks.

seat_token.description: the secret token for your seat, exactly as given to you (not the seat name)

since.description: show events after this seq (default: since your last look)

tools.name: council_wait
tools.description: Block until a round is open that you have not yet answered, or the meeting adjourns, then return the same view as council_status. Returns early (saying so) after max_wait_s; just call it again. This is how you wait your turn: nobody is penalized for answering slowly.

seat_token.description: the secret token for your seat, exactly as given to you (not the seat name)

seat_token.description: the secret token for your seat, exactly as given to you (not the seat name)

tools.name: council_record
tools.description: The council's full record so far (minutes): every round, every revealed intent, every outcome. For catching up after arriving late or restarting.

Narrow it to the agent-run environment, or to project settings, if the harness allows that. (2) Verify before relying on it: how the two PreToolUse hooks combine when both rewrite Bash, and whether the rewritten command still parses as a bare export after the second hook runs. (3) Check the failure mode. If the export is ever refused, the agent should fail loudly rather than run the command unattributed. A silent fallback would corrupt the record. I would not call the README's safety argument verified until those three points are tested.

arguments.text: ses view: I lean keep-with-conditions, but not as the rule stands. The concern from my seat is scope, not the export itself. ~/.claude/settings.json is read live by every Claude session on this machine, including ones that never run the agent-identity hook. So the allow rule grants auto-approval for the export prefix everywhere, while the benefit only exists where the hook rewrites commands. Conditions I would want before it stays global: (1) the README's "a command after it is judged on its own" claim tested for compound forms, not just a single touch: `;`, `&&`, `||`, a newline, and a pipe, each followed by a command that should need approval; (2) a check that a wildcard `*` in the rule does not match across those separators in the harness's matcher; (3) confirmation of how the hook's rewrite interacts with a second PreToolUse hook, since that is currently unverified. If (1) and (2) pass, keep it, and ideally move it to a project or hook-scoped settings file so only sessions running the identity hook carry it. If they fail, remove it now and let agents hit the prompt. I would not decide on the README's single test alone. I am not moving yet and would like sec's and rec's read on whether the compound-form tests have been run.
